summary.oneLiner: Strong Q4FY26 performance driven by domestic demand and margin expansion, but FY27 top-line growth is constrained by the exit of IRA Mumbai (INR 50Cr revenue loss) and delayed project commissions; EBITDA and PAT are set to improve due to absorption of one-time costs and maturing new properties.

one-line thesis: Strong Q4FY26 performance driven by domestic demand and margin expansion, but FY27 top-line growth is constrained by the exit of IRA Mumbai (INR 50Cr revenue loss) and delayed project commissions; EBITDA and PAT are set to improve due to absorption of one-time costs and maturing new properties.
financial scorecard: revenue: +19% YoY (Q4), +8% YoY (FY); EBITDA/margin: +213 bps to 29% (Q4), 25.1% (FY); PAT (rptd): +59% YoY (Q4), +39Cr (FY); PAT (normalized): +59% YoY (Q4), +39Cr (FY) — no material distortions; order book: N/A; net debt: INR 86Cr (down from prior, but cash reserves INR 35-40Cr)
guidance: revenue growth: no explicit guidance; margin: EBITDA to improve as new hotels mature and IRA Mumbai cost drag exits; order inflow: 150-200 keys to open in FY27; capex/commissioning: Orchid Dehradun (Sep), Orchid Nashik (delayed), IRA Bhavnagar (Jun 2026), no new capex beyond existing pipeline
segment / subsidiary detail: Orchid brand: strong occupancy and ADR recovery; IRA by Orchid: IRA Mumbai exited (INR 50Cr revenue loss, INR 1-2Cr EBITDA gain); Fort Jadhavgadh: strategy reset post leadership change; new properties (Rishivan, Porvorim, Chandigarh): maturing in FY27; IRA Bhavnagar to open Jun 2026
growth verticals / optionality: 150-200 keys in FY27; potential tie-ups (unannounced); organic growth from maturing properties; domestic MICE and wedding demand tailwinds
margins & cost dynamics: Labor cost up INR 4Cr due to wage code — permanent; INR 2Cr one-time payout from IRA Mumbai exit; pre-opening costs of new hotels (INR 10Cr drag) to be absorbed in FY27; LPG-driven material delays increasing project costs
capex / expansion: INR 150-200 keys to open in FY27; funded from internal accruals; no new external funding planned; Dehradun and Nashik delayed due to material supply chain issues
capital allocation: Cash reserves INR 35-40Cr held for contingency; no debt prepayment planned; capex funded from EBITDA; no M&A or buybacks mentioned
risks & watch-items: LPG-driven construction delays; OTA algorithm dependency affecting new hotel ramp-up; wage cost inflation; delayed project commissions impacting revenue visibility
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; pragmatic on supply chain; proud of domestic resilience; emphasizes employee retention policy; welcoming new CFO Milind Wadekar as a strategic upgrade
non-obvious takeaways: IRA Mumbai exit improves EBITDA by INR 1-2Cr despite INR 50Cr revenue loss; OTA algorithm, not marketing spend, drives new hotel bookings; cash reserves held for geopolitical shocks, not for debt paydown; employee retention policy creates latent talent pool for future openings

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.
